newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's EAAB 96 profit up 8 pct, to issue bond.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's EAAB 96 profit up 8 pct, to issue bond.

text.p: Egypt Arab African Bank/EAAB said on Wednesday it raised net profits in calendar 1996 by eight percent to 11.506 million pounds from 10.575 million in the previous year.
The profits are equivalent to about 1.5 pounds for each of the 7.5 million shares, which closed on the Egyptian stock exchange on Tuesday at 24.55 pounds.

The bank said in a published announcement that an extraordinary meeting of the general assembly approved a proposal to issue bonds worth 150 million pounds ($44 million) to finance an expansion in operations. It did not elaborate.
"The bonds will be issued in early July, 1997 and will pay out floating interest," a brokerage source told Reuters. He said other details would be available at the time of issuance.
The bank's total balance sheet rose to 1.3 billion pounds at the end of 1996 from 1.16 billion a year ago, the bank added.
Total revenue also increased to 111.36 million pounds from 108.1 million in 1995.

Call deposits in 1996 rose to 56.9 million pounds from 44.9 million in 1995. Shareholders' funds at the end of December, 1996 were worth 128.31 million pounds against 93.71 million at the end of the previous year.

The Arab African International Bank holds 49 percent in EAAB, banking sources said. Other shareholders include Egyptian Re-Insurance, 9.46 percent, AAIB's pension fund, 7.19, Mansour Maghrabi for Investment, 6.99 and individuals, 25.45.
